reports.title: Cardinal Health Reports First Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Results and Raises Outlook

lines: Cardinal Health is raising its fiscal year 2027 guidance for non-GAAP diluted EPS to $12.80 to $13.00, from the previous range of $12.40 to $12.60.
3Growth rates for fiscal year 2027 guidance based upon adjusted fiscal year 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $10.95, which excludes the fiscal year 2026 benefit from IEEPA tariff refund.

desk.headline: Revenue up 5% to $67.5bn; adjusted EPS up 28% to $3.26, beat; FY27 EPS outlook raised to $12.80–13.00
results: Revenue rose 5% to $67.5bn and adjusted EPS jumped 28% to $3.26, helped by higher profit, fewer shares and a lower tax rate.
The drug distribution and specialty unit grew revenue 6% to $62.6bn and profit 17% to $783m on brand, specialty and generics.
The medical products unit was the weak spot: revenue flat at $3.2bn and profit down 28% to $33m on distribution and currency pressure.
Nuclear, at-home and logistics businesses ('Other') grew revenue 7% and profit 16% to $193m.
The company finished a $500m share buyback in the quarter; adjusted free cash flow was $1.6bn.

guidance.summary: Cardinal raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS range to $12.80–13.00 from $12.40–12.60, and lifted profit growth targets for its pharma and 'Other' units. It gives no GAAP outlook.

points: Specialty sales grew 18%, led by cancer and urology drugs; weight-loss (GLP-1) drugs added about 5 points to revenue growth.
Government drug price cuts under the Inflation Reduction Act took about 4 points off revenue growth.
Higher oil-linked costs tied to the Iran conflict push medical unit profit towards the low end of its unchanged $200–220m range; Q2 should look like Q1.
Management expects earnings growth to slow in Q2 and Q3 before picking up in Q4.
The CVS distribution deal is being renewed to June 2032; possible 340B reimbursement changes were flagged as an uncertainty.
call.source: Zacks, 'CAH Q1 Earnings Call Highlights', 6 Nov 2026

watch: Whether the medical products unit improves from Q3 as promised despite higher oil-linked costs.
The pace of specialty and GLP-1 growth against drug price cuts under the Inflation Reduction Act.
Closing of the AdaptHealth Diabetes Health deal, expected in fiscal Q3.
